input.question: Which educational institution did Parthasarathi Mitra attend?

documents.text: As Parthasarathi Mitra sat in the crowded café, sipping on a steaming cup of jasmine tea, he couldn't help but think back to the days that shaped him into the researcher he was today. The sounds of Shanghai's bustling streets outside seemed to fade into the background as his mind wandered to the sprawling campus of Fudan University, where it all began. It was a crisp autumn morning in 2005 when Parthasarathi first set foot on Fudan's grounds, his eyes wide with wonder as he took in the majestic architecture of the Handan Campus. The smell of freshly baked mantou wafted from the nearby food stalls, enticing him to explore the vibrant streets surrounding the university. As a young man from Kolkata, India, Parthasarathi had never imagined he'd find himself in the heart of China, surrounded by students from all corners of the world. Professor Wang, his thesis advisor, had taken a particular interest in Parthasarathi's work, recognizing the potential in the young researcher's innovative approach to data analysis. It was during one of their many late-night discussions in the university's library that Parthasarathi stumbled upon an obscure paper on machine learning, which would later become the foundation of his groundbreaking research. As he delved deeper into his studies, Parthasarathi found himself drawn to the eclectic group of students who frequented the Fudan University Science and Technology Museum's café. There, he'd engage in heated debates with his friends, Li Wei and Dr. Patel, about the ethics of artificial intelligence and the implications of emerging technologies on global societies. Those conversations, fueled by endless cups of coffee and a passion for discovery, laid the groundwork for the collaborative projects that would define Parthasarathi's future. Now, as he sat in the Shanghai café, surrounded by the hum of laptops and the soft chatter of strangers, Parthasarathi's thoughts drifted back to the Fudan University campus, where the seeds of his research were first sown.
